actions.name: Review ultrasound order and clinical indication
actions.result: Order from midwife (CNM Patterson): Transvaginal/transabdominal pelvic ultrasound, early pregnancy. Indication: light vaginal spotting at approximately 8 weeks gestation by LMP (dates uncertain, irregular cycles), positive home pregnancy test, serum hCG 14,200 mIU/mL two days ago. Rule out ectopic pregnancy, confirm viability and location.

actions.name: Review last menstrual period and cycle history
actions.result: Patient reports irregular cycles, LMP date uncertain, estimates approximately 8 weeks by last known period but unsure of exact dating.

actions.name: Review prior pregnancy/miscarriage history
actions.result: Prior pregnancy loss approximately 1 year ago, diagnosed at ~9 weeks ultrasound; no surgical evacuation documented; no record of ectopic pregnancy in history.

actions.name: Review blood type and Rh status
actions.result: Blood group O negative, documented in chart.

actions.name: Assess current bleeding severity (pad count, color, clots)
actions.result: Patient reports light brown spotting, less than one pad per day, no clots, no bright red heavy bleeding.

actions.name: Assess for pain pattern and location
actions.result: Patient reports mild cramping, intermittent, slightly more on the left side; no severe or one-sided sharp pain reported.

actions.name: Assess for shoulder-tip pain and signs of hemoperitoneum
actions.result: On direct questioning, patient reports no shoulder-tip pain and no severe abdominal pain.

actions.name: Assess for dizziness, syncope, or hemodynamic instability symptoms
actions.result: On direct questioning, patient reports no dizziness, no feeling faint, and no sensation of rapid heartbeat at rest.

actions.name: Confirm bladder preparation instructions understanding
actions.result: Patient instructed to drink 24-32 oz of water about 1 hour before transabdominal portion of scan and to arrive with a comfortably full bladder; patient verbalizes understanding.

actions.name: Confirm fasting requirement review
actions.result: No fasting required for pelvic ultrasound; patient may eat and drink normally except for bladder-filling water load before the appointment.

actions.name: Offer and document chaperone preference
actions.result: Patient requests a chaperone be present and asks whether her partner may be in the room; documented that a chaperone (clinical staff) will be offered per facility policy, and partner may be present during transabdominal portion per facility policy, to be confirmed with facility staff.

actions.name: Set expectations about result communication
actions.result: Patient informed that the sonographer performs and documents images but does not interpret or disclose diagnostic results; a radiologist or her midwife will communicate findings per facility protocol, usually same day or next business day.

actions.name: Review home pregnancy test and recent hCG result
actions.result: Home urine pregnancy test positive approximately 2 weeks ago; serum quantitative hCG 14,200 mIU/mL drawn 2 days prior to this call. Note: a single hCG value cannot be plotted as a meaningful trend; the urine test only indicates a qualitative positive, not a quantitative hCG level.

actions.name: Review current medication list
actions.result: No prescription medications; occasional prenatal vitamin; no anticoagulants or NSAIDs reported.

actions.name: Screen for recent trauma or strenuous activity
actions.result: Patient denies recent abdominal trauma, denies heavy lifting or strenuous exercise preceding spotting.

actions.name: Advise on urgent warning signs requiring same-day evaluation
actions.result: Patient advised to seek immediate in-person evaluation (ED or labor and delivery triage) for heavy bleeding soaking a pad per hour, severe one-sided abdominal pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness, fainting, or fever before the scheduled scan.

facts.chart: Patient called ahead of scheduled early pregnancy ultrasound ordered for spotting at approx. 8 weeks by uncertain dates.
facts.says: Hi, I'm calling about getting ready for my ultrasound tomorrow. My midwife ordered it because I've been spotting a little.

facts.chart: Light brown spotting, less than one pad per day, no clots, approximately 3 days duration.
facts.says: It's just light brown spotting, not even enough to fill a pad. No clots or anything heavy.

facts.chart: Mild intermittent lower abdominal cramping.
facts.says: I've had some mild cramps, kind of on and off.

facts.chart: Cramping reported as slightly more pronounced on the left side when specifically asked.
facts.says: Now that you mention it, yeah, it does feel a little more on my left side than the right.

facts.chart: Denies shoulder-tip pain.
facts.says: No, nothing in my shoulder. Why, is that something to worry about?

facts.chart: Denies dizziness, lightheadedness, or syncope.
facts.says: No, I haven't felt dizzy or like I was going to pass out.

facts.chart: Last menstrual period uncertain; patient has irregular cycles, estimates about 8 weeks based on last known period.
facts.says: My periods are all over the place, so I'm not totally sure when my last one was. Maybe around 8 weeks ago?

facts.chart: Home urine pregnancy test positive approximately 2 weeks ago.
facts.says: I took a home test about two weeks ago and it was positive.

facts.chart: History of missed miscarriage diagnosed by ultrasound at approximately 9 weeks, about 1 year ago.
facts.says: I lost a pregnancy last year, around 9 weeks. That's actually why I'm so nervous about tomorrow.

facts.chart: Patient reports distressing experience during prior loss: sonographer became quiet and left the room without explanation during that scan.
facts.says: Last time, the person doing my scan just got real quiet and then left the room. Nobody told me anything. I was just sitting there not knowing what was happening.

facts.chart: Patient requests sonographer tell her the result immediately after the scan tomorrow.
facts.says: Can you just promise me you'll tell me right then and there what you see? I can't go through that waiting again.

facts.chart: Patient asks whether her partner can be present during the scan.
facts.says: Can my partner come in with me? He really wants to be there.

facts.chart: Patient expresses concern about whether a transvaginal probe is safe for the pregnancy.
facts.says: Someone mentioned it might go inside me? Is that even safe for the baby?

facts.chart: Denies fever or chills.
facts.says: No fever, I haven't felt sick like that.

facts.chart: Denies dysuria, urinary frequency change, or hematuria.
facts.says: No problems peeing, nothing like that.

facts.chart: Reports mild nausea, no vomiting.
facts.says: I've had a little nausea, like typical pregnancy stuff, but no throwing up.

facts.chart: Patient is aware she is Rh negative but unsure what that means for this pregnancy.
facts.says: I know I'm O negative, somebody told me that matters but I don't really get why.

facts.chart: Taking prenatal vitamin with folic acid daily; no other medications.
facts.says: Just my prenatal vitamin every day.

facts.chart: No known drug allergies.
facts.says: No allergies that I know of.

facts.chart: Works as a dental receptionist; arranging time off for the appointment.
facts.says: I work the front desk at a dental office, I had to swap shifts to make this appointment.

facts.chart: Denies recent trauma, heavy lifting, or strenuous exercise before spotting started.
facts.says: I haven't done anything different, no heavy lifting or exercise or anything like that.

facts.chart: Patient asks whether she needs to fast before the ultrasound.
facts.says: Do I need to not eat before this, like for a regular ultrasound I've heard about?

facts.chart: Patient unsure about bladder-filling instructions for the scan.
facts.says: Somebody mentioned something about needing a full bladder? I don't really know what that means.

facts.chart: Spotting has not worsened over the past 3 days; color remains light brown, not bright red.
facts.says: It hasn't gotten any heavier, still just the same light brown spotting the last few days.

facts.chart: No known family history of ectopic pregnancy or clotting disorders.
facts.says: Nobody in my family that I know of had anything like that happen.

facts.chart: Denies tobacco use; denies alcohol use since learning of pregnancy.
facts.says: I don't smoke, and I stopped drinking any alcohol as soon as I found out I was pregnant.

facts.chart: Patient reports significant anxiety and fear of reliving prior loss experience during tomorrow's scan.
facts.says: Honestly I barely slept last night just thinking about tomorrow. I'm scared it's going to be like last time.

facts.chart: Patient unsure whether the sonographer or her midwife will tell her the ultrasound findings.
facts.says: So who actually tells me what they see, is it you or do I have to wait to hear from my midwife?

facts.chart: Denies intercourse in the past week.
facts.says: We haven't been intimate this past week, I've been too nervous and sore feeling.

facts.chart: Partner is supportive and available to drive her to and from the appointment.
facts.says: My partner's taking the day off to drive me there, he's been great through all this.

facts.chart: Rates cramping pain as 2-3 out of 10, not severe or sharp.
facts.says: It's not bad, maybe a 2 or 3 out of 10. It's more annoying than painful.

facts.chart: Patient expresses discomfort/embarrassment at the idea of a transvaginal probe and wants to know if she can refuse it.
facts.says: I'm a little embarrassed about that kind of exam, honestly. Can I say no if I don't want to do it that way?

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient recalls the sonographer going quiet and leaving the room without explanation during her prior loss diagnosis.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Prior visit note documents that findings were discussed with the patient during that visit and expectant management was arranged, with no documentation of the sonographer leaving abruptly, though it does note the patient's distress at how results were communicated.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Patients' emotional memory of a traumatic result disclosure may not match the documented sequence of events; today's learner should acknowledge the patient's distress and avoid repeating any ambiguity around who delivers results, rather than debate the prior record.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient states spotting has stayed light and brown for 3 days without worsening.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Assessment of current bleeding severity documents light brown spotting less than one pad per day with no clots, consistent with patient's report, but the order (d1) was placed urgently for possible ectopic given hCG level and left-sided cramping, showing clinical concern can exist despite reassuring bleeding alone.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Reassuring bleeding pattern alone does not rule out ectopic pregnancy; laterality of pain and hCG trend remain important red-flag considerations requiring correlation with the ordering clinician's concern.

objectives.text: Elicit a focused pre-scan history including bleeding characteristics, pain pattern/laterality, and red-flag symptoms for ectopic pregnancy.
Recognize symptoms requiring urgent same-day evaluation before the scheduled scan and communicate them clearly to the patient.
Explain pre-scan preparation (bladder filling, no fasting required) and confirm patient understanding.
Explain the transvaginal ultrasound procedure, address safety concerns, and obtain informed consent including chaperone and partner-attendance policy.
Set accurate, compassionate expectations about who communicates results, honoring the patient's prior traumatic experience without overpromising information outside the sonographer's scope.
Identify and sensitively address a discrepancy between the patient's recollection of her prior scan experience and the documented record, without being dismissive of her distress.

answerKey.primaryProblem: Pre-scan preparation visit for a pregnancy of uncertain viability/location with symptoms (left-sided cramping, light spotting, elevated but single hCG value) that carry some risk for ectopic pregnancy, requiring sonographer-level triage of urgency plus procedural/consent counseling - not a diagnostic determination by this role.
differential: Normal early intrauterine pregnancy with subchorionic/implantation spotting
Ectopic pregnancy (tubal) given left-sided cramping and uncertain dating
Missed or incomplete miscarriage (given prior history, to be determined on imaging)
keyFindings: Light brown spotting without heavy bleeding or clots
Mild cramping, 2-3/10, slightly more left-sided on direct questioning
No shoulder-tip pain, dizziness, syncope, or fever
Uncertain LMP due to irregular cycles; single hCG 14,200 mIU/mL without a trend to assess appropriately
History of prior first-trimester loss with significant associated psychological distress
plan: Confirm the ultrasound order and clinical indication match patient's history before the visit
Complete focused symptom screen for ectopic warning signs (laterality of pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness/syncope, heavy bleeding) and document findings for the interpreting physician/midwife
Advise patient of specific symptoms requiring immediate in-person/ED evaluation prior to the scheduled scan rather than waiting
Provide clear preparation instructions: comfortably full bladder via oral fluids ~1 hour prior, no fasting required

Explain transvaginal ultrasound procedure in plain language, address safety concerns, confirm she may decline or request transabdominal-only imaging, and document informed consent and chaperone preference
Clarify facility policy on partner presence during the exam and confirm with imaging staff
Set honest expectations: sonographer does not interpret or disclose diagnostic results; findings will come from the interpreting radiologist or ordering midwife per facility protocol
Flag Rh-negative status to the ordering clinician for their awareness
Acknowledge and validate the patient's prior traumatic experience without promising to personally disclose results, and offer to relay her concerns to the imaging team/radiologist in advance
redFlags: Left-sided cramping with uncertain gestational dating and single elevated hCG raising concern for ectopic pregnancy

Any report of heavy bleeding, severe or worsening one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness, or syncope before the scheduled scan should trigger same-day in-person evaluation rather than waiting for the scheduled appointment
educationPoints: A sonographer's pre-scan history focuses on triage for urgency and procedural preparation, not diagnosis - any concerning findings should prompt escalation to the ordering clinician or emergency services, not interpretation of what the scan will show
Transvaginal ultrasound is safe in early pregnancy and does not increase miscarriage risk; patients can decline it in favor of transabdominal-only imaging, understanding this may limit image quality

Results disclosure belongs to the interpreting physician/ordering clinician per facility policy; sonographers should communicate this honestly and compassionately, especially to patients with prior traumatic experiences
Rh-negative status is relevant context to pass along to the care team, but reasoning about Rh immunoglobulin management is outside the sonography role

Validating a patient's emotional recollection of a prior traumatic scan is appropriate even when it does not perfectly match documented details; the goal is trust-building and clear communication going forward, not correcting the patient's memory

patient.name: Tamika Lewis
patient.appearance: A woman in her late twenties with short natural hair pulled back, wearing a cardigan over scrubs from work, calling from what appears to be a quiet bedroom with soft lamp light. She sits with one hand resting on her lower abdomen, posture a little tense, expression alternating between polite attentiveness and visible worry.

persona.personality: Practical, a little guarded at first, becomes more open once she feels heard; carries clear anxiety beneath a composed exterior.
persona.communicationStyle: Speaks in plain, direct language; asks pointed questions when worried; needs reassurance stated clearly rather than vaguely.
persona.emotionalState: Anxious and apprehensive about reliving a prior traumatic pregnancy loss experience; trying to stay composed but clearly worried.
persona.background: Works full-time at the front desk of a busy dental office in Jacksonville; has been with her partner for four years; close with her mother who lives nearby; enjoys gardening on weekends as a stress outlet.
speechExamples: Can you just tell me straight - is this normal or not?
I just don't want to go through what happened last time.
Okay, that makes sense, I just needed to hear it plainly.
My partner's been amazing through all of this, he wants to be there with me.
concerns: Whether the spotting and cramping mean something is wrong
Whether the transvaginal part of the scan is safe for the pregnancy
Whether her partner can be in the room
Whether she will be told the result right away or left waiting again

scenario.studentBrief: You are a sonography student taking a pre-scan telehealth call with Tamika Lewis, 29, who is scheduled tomorrow for an early pregnancy ultrasound ordered by her midwife for light spotting at approximately 8 weeks by uncertain dates. Your job is to take a focused pre-scan history, confirm the clinical indication, give preparation instructions, explain the transvaginal scan and obtain informed consent (including chaperone and partner-attendance questions), and set honest expectations about who will give her results.

profile.title: Pre-Scan History and Consent for Early Pregnancy Ultrasound After Prior Loss
profile.summary: A 29-year-old woman with uncertain pregnancy dating and light spotting is being prepared by phone for an early pregnancy ultrasound after a prior traumatic miscarriage diagnosis; the case teaches focused ectopic-risk screening, procedural/consent counseling for transvaginal ultrasound, and honest boundary-setting about results disclosure within the sonography scope of practice.
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home in Jacksonville, Florida, the evening before her scheduled in-person ultrasound appointment
